Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old female presents with a new, severe, left-sided throbbing headache with photophobia for one day, no prior similar episodes, and no concerning associated symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Severe headache for 1 day
  - Onset: Yesterday morning, began upon waking
  - Duration: Ongoing for about 24 hours
  - Progression: Throbbing, intense pain, comes and goes (never fully resolves but fluctuates in severity)
  - Location: Mainly left side of head
  - Character: Throbbing, intense, sensitive to light (photophobia), worsened in bright rooms or sunlight, somewhat improved when lying down
  - No complete relief; partially fades at times
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Worse in bright/lighted places, improved when lying down
- Associated symptoms:
  - Denies visual disturbances, abnormal smells or tastes
  - No nausea or vomiting
  - Eating and drinking normally
  - No prior history of headaches
  - Denies fever, coryzal (cold) symptoms, sore ears, or skin changes
  - Denies limb weakness, numbness, or tingling
  - No symptoms on position change, coughing, or sneezing
  - No recent illness or identified triggers except possible work-related stress
- Menstrual cycle: No connection to cycle; last period ~1 week ago

Past Medical History:
- No significant past medical conditions or recent hospital admissions/operations reported
- Medications:
  - Microgynon (contraceptive pill), started 6 years ago, no significant side effects reported
  - Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented) used for current headache
- Allergies:
  - Aspirin (causes marked nausea)
- No current use of NSAIDs; previously tolerated Ibuprofen/Naproxen

Social History:
- Lives with housemates/friends
- Alcohol: Occasional, a few drinks at weekends
- Smoking: Denies use
- Recreational drugs: Denies use
- No financial or lifestyle risk factors mentioned

Family History:
- Mother has hypertension and a history of migraines

Physical Examination:
- No physical examination or vital signs documented

Investigations:
- No investigations ordered or results discussed
- Blood pressure reportedly normal six months ago at last check, no recent measurement

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute severe headache (first episode, possible migraine)
  - Assessment: Throbbing, severe, left-sided headache with photophobia, no neurological symptoms, no prior headache history; features consistent with migraine, but first episode
  - Plan:
    - Trial of NSAID (Ibuprofen) in addition to Paracetamol
    - Maintain good hydration
    - Monitor symptoms closely
    - Warning signs for report: Persisting or worsening headache, fever, rash, neurological symptoms (weakness, visual changes), persistent or recurrent headaches, headaches associated with menstrual cycle, or other changes
    - Follow up if above warning signs occur or if symptoms do not resolve
    - Arrange blood pressure check if not done recently
    - Obtain home thermometer to monitor for fever

General plan items:
- Advise follow-up if symptoms worsen/new features develop
- Longer-term headache management discussion if headaches persist or become recurrent

Quality checks (document_quality):

● Missing clinically expected elements:
  - Comprehensive allergy list beyond Aspirin
  - Medications reconciliation beyond contraceptive and Paracetamol
  - Documentation of vital signs (temperature, blood pressure, etc.)
  - Objective physical examination findings
● Internal conflicts: None noted
● Transcript quality: Clear; no notable audio issues, but some conversational repetition and minimal background information provided.
